Subject: Outbound policy questions for Private Endpoint deployment

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for taking our Private deployment review. A couple of follow-ups from our security and networking teams as we put together the firewall change request:

- Can you confirm the minimum set of outbound IPs we need to allow for Redwood control plane callbacks (status, heartbeat, metrics)? We need static entries for our perimeter firewall.
- For runtime inference egress (customer model fetches, telemetry, and optional plugin webhooks), is Redwood able to operate with a hostname/SNI-based allowlist or do you require fixed IPs?
- How often (if at all) do Redwood-managed egress IPs rotate? If ephemeral, what is the rotation window and notification method?
- Does Redwood support DNS-over-TLS or DoH to avoid cleartext DNS when we resolve Redwood endpoints from our on-prem network?
- Finally, procurement asked for any template or form we can fill that lists required network ports, attachment of proof-of-evidence (SOC2 report), and a short justification for exceptions.

I'm attaching our procurement form so you can populate the network fields where possible.

Thanks,

Hi Amit — great questions. Looping in Laura (Network SIG) and Markus (Private Deployments) to make sure we cover ops and procurement items. Below is a concise, operational-first response and a short checklist you can drop into your firewall change ticket. I also attached our lightweight "egress spec sheet" to populate the procurement form.

Short answers up front:
- Control plane: we provide a small set of stable egress CIDRs for control-plane telemetry and management. Those are suitable for firewall allowlisting and we can provide /24 granularity where required.
- Runtime egress: Redwood supports both SNI/hostname allowlisting and IP-based allowlisting. For strict regulatory customers we recommend a dedicated static egress pool (reserved NAT) that you can allowlist; otherwise SNI-based allowlisting plus DNS validation is commonly used.
- IP rotation: the default managed egress pool is ephemeral and can rotate with a 7–30 day window depending on customer profile and load. For customers who need immutability, we offer a static egress allocation as an add-on (no rotation).
- DNS transport: we support DoT (DNS-over-TLS) for names that require encrypted DNS resolution between your resolver and Redwood's resolvers. We also have guidance for using an internal forwarding resolver to maintain split-horizon behavior.

Firewall change ticket checklist (copy/paste friendly):
- Control-plane allowlist: [REDACTED] — request: allow TCP 443 to Redwood control CIDRs (we will provide exact CIDRs in a follow-up).
- Runtime: option A — allow by FQDN/SNI (recommended) OR option B — allow dedicated static egress CIDR(s) (add-on).
- DNS: allow outbound to your DNS forwarder / DoT endpoint; if using Redwood DoT endpoint allow TCP 853 to the provided hostnames.
- TLS: enforce SNI validation for outbound webhooks; for control-plane mTLS is available as an option.
- Monitoring: allow egress to our metrics endpoint for customer telemetry if you opt in (we can use a private endpoint).

Next actions from Redwood:
1) We will send a short evidence bundle (SOC2 summary + network topology excerpt).
2) Markus will follow up with the exact control-plane CIDRs and the pricing note for a static egress pool.
3) If you confirm which external FQDNs/webhook destinations you need allowed, we can validate whether SNI-only is sufficient or if IPs are required.

I've attached the redwood-egress-spec-sheet.pdf for the procurement form.

Regards,
Chloe Martin

Chloe — thanks for the clear rundown, that helps a lot. Two follow-ups from our side:

- Procurement insists on CIDRs for the initial firewall window. Can you provide the control-plane prefixes at /24 granularity? If you have a "static egress" SKU, send the exact ranges and confirm whether they are subject to rotation after contract signing.
- For runtime webhook destinations, we prefer SNI-based controls but some of our appliances only accept IP lists. If Redwood can do a hybrid where control-plane uses static egress and runtime uses SNI, that would solve our compliance gating.
- On DNS: we will be using an internal resolver that does split-horizon. If Redwood supports DoT for resolving Redwood-specific hostnames through a dedicated endpoint, that would be preferred.

Attached the filled-ish procurement form with the sections we couldn't complete. If you can populate network fields (CIDRs, ports, SNI names) we can move to firewall change and procurement sign-off.

Amit — jumping back in with concrete next steps and a recommended configuration that balances your procurement needs and operational flexibility.

Decision proposal (recommended):
- Control plane: provide three static /24 CIDRs (attached in the internal evidence bundle) for allowlisting. These are part of the Redwood control-plane contract and will not rotate during the initial 12-month term. We can include rotation clauses in the SOW for long-term engagements.
- Runtime egress: adopt a hybrid model.
  - Option 1 (recommended): runtime uses SNI/hostname allowlist for general traffic; you only need to allow TLS 443 to FQDNs we provide. This keeps NAT churn low and eases ops.
  - Option 2: if specific appliances require IPs, provision a small number of static egress CIDRs as a paid add-on; these will be reserved for your tenant and do not rotate.
- DNS: we will provide a dedicated DoT endpoint that your internal resolver can forward Redwood-specific queries to (preserving split-horizon). Allow TCP 853 to dot.redwood-inference.com.
- mTLS & webhook security: for webhook destinations that require higher assurance, we recommend mTLS and include signed client certificates.

Action items and owners:
- Redwood (Markus): share exact control-plane CIDRs and the short evidence pack (SOC2 excerpt, network diagram) by 2026-10-09.
- InfraOps (Amit): confirm which runtime webhook FQDNs you need and whether your firewalls can accept SNI-only rules by 2026-10-11.
- Redwood (Chloe): populate the procurement form we received and return the file for procurement intake by 2026-10-09.

I'm attaching the finalized redwood-egress-spec-sheet.pdf (with the control-plane placeholders filled) and the procurement form we started. Once you confirm, I can trigger the legal/SOW DocuSign for the static egress add-on if you choose that path.

Thanks — we'll stay on this until procurement signs off.
